title: Ordinal Numbers
description: Learn Ordinal Numbers with interactive diagrams, worked examples, and practice tests for Grade 2 students.

topics.title: Ordinal Numbers
topics.concept:
While regular numbers (like 1, 2, 3) tell us how many objects there are in total, ordinal numbers tell us the exact position, rank, or order of something in a list. They answer the question: "Which one?"

  • First to Twentieth (1^{\text{st}} to 20^{\text{th}}): In Grade 2, we expand our positional language beyond the top ten, learning to read, write, and spell the positions all the way from 1^{\text{st}} to 20^{\text{th}}.
  • Ranks, Lists, and Queues: When people stand in a straight line (a queue), the person at the front is 1^{\text{st}} (first), the next is 2^{\text{nd}} (second), and so on. We use the exact same concept to talk about positions in a race (ranks) or items on a page from top to bottom (lists).
  • Turns and Schedules: Ordinal numbers help keep daily life organized! We use them to talk about turns in a game ("It is your second turn") or matching schedules ("The science fair is on the fifth day of the month").

examples.problem: Twelve children are standing in a single file line waiting for the school bus. If Sam is standing directly behind the 9^{\text{th}} child, what is Sam's ordinal position from the front of the line?
examples.solution:
1. Visualize or track the position sequence from the front: 1^{\text{st}}, 2^{\text{nd}}, 3^{\text{th}}, \dots, 9^{\text{th}}.
  2. "Directly behind" means Sam is next in order after the 9^{\text{th}} spot.
  3. The position that immediately follows 9^{\text{th}} is the 10^{\text{th}} spot.
Answer: Tenth (10^{\text{th}})

recap: Ordinal numbers always end with special suffix letter flags: -st (1), -nd (2), -rd (3), or -th (4 to 20).
When finding positions from the front of a line or a finish mark, count from left to right or top to bottom.
Watch out for tricky spellings like fifth, ninth, and twelfth.
